newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude weaker, differentials under pressure.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude weaker, differentials under pressure.

text.p: Asian crude prices fell on Monday in line with the wider decline in crude futures prices and weak demand kept differentials under pressure.
Trading remained cautious as players assessed the market.
Indications for the benchmark Minas market came down as a Japanese refinery paid around ICP +20 cents for 250,000 barrels.
That was lower than a deal last week at ICP +40 cents, but still did not surprise market players.
China buyers remained quiet amid refinery turnarounds and Japan utility demand was also light, prompting some Japanese traders to back out term barrels onto the spot market.
Tapis paper fell a moderate 10 cents on Monday to $21.40/$21.55 per barrel after London April Brent shed 29 cents on Friday to close at $19.79. SIMEX April Brent fell three cents to $19.76 on Monday.
Traders said a deal for a cargo of Umm Shaif, which emerged on Friday, was possibly part of a swap for Oman.

Both were exchanged at one cent premium to their official selling prices and involved a European major and a Japanese refiner, traders said. This continued the flurry of swap deals for MidEast grades so far for April.
Three April Dubai deals emerged with a U.S. major paying full-month quotes plus 39 cents for two cargos of Dubai, and a South Korean refinery paying first-half March quotes plus one cent.
The 80,000 bpd Griffin oil field restarted production on Sunday after bad weather forced a three-day shut in, while Cossack was expected to resume operations later on Monday.
